bullets.title: NVDA: Roadmap intact confirmed; Morgan Stanley NDR highlights accelerating growth & Anthropic compute share nearing 50%
bullets.body: After circulating expert-call reports of another Rubin delay, NVIDIA confirmed to staff that its roadmap is intact per multiple sell-side sources. Morgan Stanley's NDR note cited NVDA CEO describing three growth drivers—AI labs, hyperscalers, neoclouds/enterprise—with growth rates accelerating even as revenue approaches $100B/quarter. Anthropic's share of compute running on NVIDIA chips has risen to nearly 50%, per Morgan Stanley. A separate supply-chain note flagged that Micron initially failed on Rubin pin-speed specs, causing NVDA to reduce targets, allowing ecosystem partners to ship.

bullets.title: META: +11% in two days on Muse Spark AI model, Iris chip & 14GW compute plan; KeyBanc raises PT to $790
bullets.body: Meta surged ~11% over two days—the biggest two-day gain since April 2025—after unveiling Muse Spark 1.1 (matching or beating Anthropic/Claude at 25% cheaper pricing), announcing September production start for in-house Iris AI chip (designed with AVGO, made by TSMC), and committing to double compute capacity to 14GW by 2027 with implied capex of $240-275B. META also launched Muse Image, began charging via Model API, and disclosed plans to sell excess capacity as a neocloud. KeyBanc raised PT to $790 (20x 2028E P/E); Mizuho upgraded to Outperform. The stock reclaimed its 200-day moving average by the widest margin since January.

bullets.title: MU: $250B US capex commitment through 2035; NY fab concrete poured; SK Hynix CEO warns supply crunch past 2030
bullets.body: Micron raised its planned U.S. manufacturing investment from $200B to $250B+, poured the first concrete at its New York DRAM megafab in Clay, and signed a strategic customer agreement with Ford. SK Hynix's CEO separately stated 2027 will be the worst year for memory supply in industry history and that the shortage could persist past 2030. Analysts including Mizuho and JPM see MU benefiting structurally; one analyst noted MU will likely earn more in 2026 than the prior 35 years combined. DRAM contract prices are tracking +20-30% QoQ in 3Q26.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU loses gatekeeper challenge; sues OpenAI over trade secrets; $30B AVGO deal through 2031
bullets.body: Apple lost its EU DMA gatekeeper appeal (potential 10% revenue fine for non-compliance), then filed a lawsuit in federal court against OpenAI alleging misappropriation of trade secrets—including claims that OpenAI's chief hardware officer directed former Apple employees to bring confidential hardware files, and that Apple alleges OpenAI hired 400+ Apple staff. Separately, Apple expanded its multiyear Broadcom agreement beyond $30B through 2031 to produce 15B+ US-made chips, including a new custom AI datacenter ASIC expected to ramp ~2029/2030. Hedgeye added AAPL as a new short with 23% downside target.

bullets.title: GOOGL: KeyBanc raises PT to $445 on durable Cloud/Search momentum; supply fatigue in bond markets
bullets.body: KeyBanc raised its GOOGL price target to $445 (25x 2028E P/E), modeling 2Q Cloud revenue of $23.4B (+72% YoY) and a total backlog expected to surpass $480B. Separately, JPMorgan's credit team downgraded GOOGL bonds from Overweight citing growing leverage, and flagged Google's $85B equity issuance as peaking financial asset prices. Google's quarterly interest expense also hit $500M—up 15x year-over-year—as AI buildout accelerates. UK regulators designated GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN, and ORCL as critical third parties subject to direct financial regulatory oversight.

bullets.title: MSFT: GPT-5.6 becomes default in 365 Copilot; Xbox cuts 4,800 jobs; $190B capex headwinds noted
bullets.body: Microsoft integrated GPT-5.6 as the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot and is separately routing some Excel/Outlook AI prompts to proprietary MAI models to cut costs. Microsoft also cut 4,800 jobs—mostly Xbox, with four studios going independent. On the credit side, JPMorgan downgraded MSFT bonds to Underweight citing heavy 2026 capex (~$190B) and unfunded gap vs. peers who have all tapped bond markets. UK regulators also designated MSFT a critical financial-sector supplier subject to direct oversight effective July 13.

bullets.title: AMZN: $25B bond sale for AI capex; AWS estimates raised; GOOGL, MSFT designated UK critical suppliers
bullets.body: Amazon launched a $25B eight-tranche bond sale—its fourth debt raise YTD (totaling ~$53B)—to fund AI infrastructure. JPMorgan raised AWS revenue estimates to +32% YoY in 2Q and +33% for FY26, with total capex revised to $200B in 2026 and $294B in 2027. Amazon's DSP continued gaining digital advertising share. The UK government also designated AMZN (alongside MSFT, GOOGL, ORCL) as a critical third party to the financial system, with Bank of England/PRA/FCA oversight beginning July 13.

bullets.title: AVGO: $30B+ Apple deal through 2031 extended to include new AI/datacenter ASIC; META ASIC ramp underway
bullets.body: Broadcom extended its multiyear partnership with Apple beyond $30B through 2031, expanding scope to include a custom Server ASIC for Apple Private Cloud Compute (ramp expected ~2029/2030) alongside RF components. Separately, META's ASIC (branded 'Iris') enters production in September via AVGO design and TSMC manufacturing, with a multi-GW commitment. Wolfe Research came away from management meetings bullish on FY28 XPV-driven revenue; stock was downgraded to hold by Erste Group but remains a top pick at multiple other desks.

bullets.title: NFLX: Engagement declining; exploring live TV and bundles; JPMorgan keeps OW, PT $118; Citi cuts to $100
bullets.body: Multiple reports describe Netflix experiencing declining engagement (watch time, completion rates, global DAU down 6% YoY) despite healthy subscriber retention. Netflix is exploring always-on live TV channels, bundling Peacock in-app, and potentially bidding on 2030/2034 FIFA World Cup rights. JPMorgan maintained OW with $118 PT, modeling 2Q inline with guidance; Citi cut PT to $100 (from $115) citing multiple compression risk. Separately, Netflix, Paramount, Sony, and Versant have been in early discussions about acquiring Letterboxd at ~$250M per StreetAccount.

bullets.title: TSM: JPM raises PT to NT$3100 on AI demand; CoWoS capacity revised up 9-11%; 2Q expected to beat
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised TSMC's Jun-27 price target to NT$3100 (6% above prior) and lifted FY26/27/28E EPS by 5%/10%/16% on AI demand acceleration. CoWoS capacity estimates were raised for the fourth time in 2026 to 115k/190k/225k wfpm by end-26/27/28. The demand-supply gap for advanced packaging has widened to ~20%. 2Q results (due July 16) expected to beat consensus, with 3Q guidance likely at +10-12% QoQ on strong AI CPU and accelerator orders. Rapidus also announced 2nm wafer pricing to undercut TSMC.

bullets.title: TSLA: Robotaxi expands to Miami unsupervised; Optimus ramp to 1,000/week by September; SPCX-TSLA combination discussed
bullets.body: Tesla launched its first non-Texas unsupervised robotaxi market in Miami with ~59 vehicles. Optimus humanoid production is targeting 1,000 units/week by September and 100K annual capacity by year-end. Elon Musk directed Tesla and SpaceX employees to evaluate Grok 4.5. JPMorgan published a note on SPCX-TSLA combination noting strategic coherence (shared AI infrastructure, $55B Texas Terafab JV) but flagging regulatory and governance hurdles.

bullets.title: HOOD: 70K+ Agentic Trading accounts opened; Robinhood Chain $633M DEX volume; leveraged SK Hynix ETFs launching Tuesday
bullets.body: Robinhood reported 70,000+ Agentic Trading accounts opened since the May launch, with the feature expanding to crypto for eligible US customers. Robinhood Chain reached $633M in DEX volume with 306.5K daily active users, and ETH bridged from Ethereum L1 grew ~10x to $100M+. Robinhood CEO also promoted the Trump Accounts initiative. Two leveraged SK Hynix ETFs (2x long SKHX, 1x short SKHZ) from Leverage Shares are set to launch Tuesday following the SK Hynix IPO.

bullets.title: SHOP: Stifel upgrades to Buy with $150 PT; BofA reinstates Buy at same target ahead of 2Q
bullets.body: Both Stifel (upgrade from hold) and Bank of America (reinstatement) issued Buy ratings on Shopify with a $150 price target each, implying ~21-22% upside. Stifel analyst Parker Lane and BofA's Tal Liani cited durable GMV growth, payments monetization expansion, and AI-driven product leverage. Q2 is expected to show 30-31% revenue growth; analysts note the stock requires at least 30% in Q2 plus mid-to-high 20% Q3 guidance to sustain momentum.

bullets.title: WULF: Surges 10%+ on $19B 20-year Anthropic data lease at Justified campus in Kentucky
bullets.body: TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic for ~401MW at Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, KY, generating ~$19B in contracted revenue. The implied annual rent of $197/kW/month exceeded Citi's prior $150/kW estimate (implied ~22% yield). WULF also sold its 50.1% Abernathy JV stake to Fluidstack for $530M to recycle capital into wholly-owned projects. Morgan Stanley raised WULF PT to $72 from $66.50. IREN also rallied on news of Anthropic's planned 1.4GW Australian data center.

bullets.title: FIG (Figma): PT cut to $28 at JPM on margin pressure; gross margins set to trough below 81% from ~90%
bullets.body: JPMorgan cut its Figma price target from $42 to $28, citing AI compute costs driving gross margins to trough below 81% medium-term (from ~90% prior year). The analysts model F2Q revenue of $359M (+44% YoY) vs. $349M guidance, and note AI credit monetization and seat expansion are revenue drivers. Jason Calacanis noted he remains 'extremely long' Figma after resolving a miscommunication. BofA also reinstated FIG at Buy with $30 PT.

bullets.title: DKNG: Indiana June GGR -38% YoY on 570bps hold-rate compression; state sports betting -18% YoY
bullets.body: Indiana June sports betting GGR fell 18% YoY (handle +15% YoY) as industry-wide hold rates declined 370bps to 9.2%. DraftKings specifically saw June GGR -38% YoY with market share declining from 37% to 36%. FanDuel GGR -24% YoY; BetMGM -31% YoY. Indiana casino GGR was approximately flat for 2Q. DraftKings is also launching in Alberta on July 13.

bullets.title: NET: Upgraded to sector outperform at Scotiabank GBM ($300 PT) on cybersecurity AI tailwind
bullets.body: Scotiabank GBM upgraded Cloudflare from sector perform to sector outperform, raising its price target to $300 from $225 (21% upside). The upgrade cites cybersecurity spending rising with frontier AI models and Cloudflare's positioning as a key beneficiary. Cloudflare also announced a research pilot with OpenAI to improve AI search indexing and answer accuracy.

bullets.title: LITE, AAOI, COHR: Optical sector weakness seen overdone by Rosenblatt; InP capacity emerging as AI bottleneck
bullets.body: Rosenblatt published a note arguing photonics short sellers lack conviction and are 'preying on fear'—expecting shorts to cover before strong earnings prints. LITE flagged InP (Indium Phosphide) capacity expansion as a transition from a sub-topic to a critical physical AI infrastructure bottleneck. Lumentum is presenting on VCSEL-based wide-parallel optical interconnects for AI networks at LightCounting on July 15. AAOI, LITE, COHR remain technically weak but analysts see the sector as a contrarian long.

bullets.title: FSLR: Deutsche Bank upgrades to Buy; PT raised to $272 from $245
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank upgraded First Solar from Hold to Buy, raising the price target to $272 (from $245), citing stronger second-half outlook, normalized 2027 estimates, and expected tariff policy clarifications. FSLR is also viewed as a key beneficiary of data center onsite power demand, with Morgan Stanley simultaneously raising its FSLR PT to $245 from $230 on robust BESS and onsite power orders.

bullets.title: FOXA: Upgraded to Buy at Rothschild & Co Redburn ($71 PT) on Roku deal valuation upside
bullets.body: Rothschild & Co Redburn upgraded Fox Corp from Neutral to Buy, raising the price target from $48 to $71 (32% upside), citing valuation and strategic upside from the Roku partnership. Fox also faces competitive pressure on World Cup broadcasting rights from Netflix, Disney, and YouTube. The stock declined modestly intraday but the upgrade maintained positive sentiment.
